name: Horny goat weed (Epimedium)
short: Case reports: fast heart rhythm with hypomania; severe muscle spasms with raised CK and creatinine; more opioid cravings on buprenorphine. A review notes possible liver toxicity of crude extracts.
text: The evidence of harm comes from individual case reports and laboratory or review data. A published case report describes tachyarrhythmia (a fast heart rhythm) and hypomania with horny goat weed (no abstract is available, so only its title is cited), and a systematic review of case reports of mania linked to herbal medicines counted one such report for horny goat weed while cautioning that causal attribution is problematic. A 33-year-old man who took an Epimedium supplement bought online for a month developed severe muscle spasms with raised creatine kinase and creatinine needing hospital admission, which improved in hospital (case report). Another case report described increased opioid cravings after a patient on buprenorphine started Herba Epimedii; the authors note that laboratory studies show the herb interacts with the liver enzyme CYP3A4, which breaks down buprenorphine, and this is the only medicine interaction named in the cited sources. A systematic review of Epimedium koreanum states that its crude extracts can result in liver toxicity; the abstract does not say whether this evidence comes from human or animal studies. A meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials (1,017 patients) of Epimedium for osteoporosis listed adverse events as a secondary outcome, but the abstract does not report adverse event results.
